claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic, multi-principal-element automotive alloy with Pt-based active sites.
Co, Ni, Bi, and Sn can be incorporated in controlled amounts into Pt(111) facets of the catalyst.
Co, Ni, Bi, and Sn doping will modify the local electronic structure of Pt(111) surface sites.
The dopants will tune the d-band center of Pt.
Dopant-induced electronic tuning will lower the activation energy for CO oxidation.
Dopant-induced electronic tuning will lower the activation energy for hydrocarbon oxidation.
The dopants will reduce the binding strength of H2O on the catalyst surface.
The dopants will reduce the binding strength of NO on the catalyst surface.
The doped catalyst will have a lower CO and hydrocarbon light-off temperature than the unmodified catalyst.
The doped catalyst will maintain greater catalytic activity in the presence of H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The doped catalyst will show less performance degradation after accelerated automotive aging than the unmodified catalyst.
Adding Co, Ni, Bi, and Sn will improve catalyst performance without increasing platinum-group-metal loading.
The predicted improvements will apply during transient exhaust operation below 150 °C with H2O and NO exposure.
The predicted improvements will persist after aging intended to represent a full vehicle lifetime.
